title: Joseph's Colorful Coat
reflectionQuestion: Even far from home, God was always with Joseph. When you go somewhere new, what helps you feel that God is near you?
kidSafetyNotes: NEW anchor (Joseph, core-launch finale). The HARD origin half that pairs with 1819 Joseph Forgives (the reconciliation); consistent with 1819 ('sent him far away to Egypt'). HARD CONTENT handled by the Joseph method (Adam 2026-06-18: heavy is OK, but do NOT make the brothers' cruelty vivid): the pit and the selling-for-silver are OMITTED -- softened to 'the brothers decided to send him away' with passing traders; show the brothers' JEALOUSY (a feeling) not violence. Lands hard on 'God was with Joseph' (the 1819-proven move, feedback_kid_not_alone_thread / feedback_kid_god_with_not_cause -- God stays WITH him in the hard thing, doesn't cause it) and points FORWARD to the rescue without spoiling it. Flag family_betrayal_softened. For a left-out / lonely child: jealousy + being sent away -> God-never-left routes a 'left out / far from home' kid to comfort. Indelible image = the colorful coat (and the coat-weaving / God-weaving-a-plan callback in the full). 'God' throughout, no Yahweh. VOICE_JAMES_BRITISH (reassuring father) -- steady warmth through hardship.

scriptureKeyVerse.text: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age, and he made him a tunic of many colors.
